_derived: DERIVED - not verbatim. RFC 9679 states its computation as a three-step numbered procedure in prose (Section 3) and its field sets as five bullet lists (Sections 4.1 to 4.5). This file is that procedure rendered as data by m-of-n/library so a test harness can read it. Cite it as derived, never as the RFC's own text (R-O-03).
source: RFC 9679, CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Key Thumbprint, December 2024

steps.output: a COSE_Key structure holding only the required parameters for the key type, as listed in §4
steps.notes: Constructs a new map. It is not a filter applied in place to the received encoding: see entry_order below, and note that the document's own full example key (source lines 416-419) is not itself in deterministic order.

steps.output: the deterministic encoding of the structure from step 1
steps.notes: RFC 9679 restates none of 4.2.1. Everything byte-level - preferred serialization of every head, definite-length strings only, and the map-key sort - is that reference.
H is a parameter of the procedure. The resulting value carries no identifier of H (see hash_function below).

hash_function.notes: A thumbprint is a bare digest. Nothing in the value, and nothing in the §5.6 ckt member, says which H produced it; only the §5.7 URI form names it. Two parties on different H never match on any key (rfc-9679#R-0040).

entry_order.stated_in_source_as: the minimum parameters in the correct order (§6), ordered essential parameters (§5.1), a specific order (§5.4)
entry_order.rule: RFC 8949 §4.2.1: map keys are sorted by the bytewise lexicographic order of their deterministic encodings.
entry_order.consequence: A positive label sorts before every negative label, so kty (1, encoded 0x01) leads and the type-specific labels follow as -1 (0x20), -2 (0x21), -3 (0x22).
entry_order.confirmed_by: the worked encoding at source lines 442-444: a4 01 02 20 01 21 5820 <x> 22 5820 <y>

excluded_labels.rule: Only the required parameters of §4 are used (rfc-9679#R-0007); every other COSE_Key parameter is excluded, whether or not the document names it.

excluded_by_silence.name: alg
excluded_by_silence.note: The string alg does not appear anywhere in RFC 9679.

excluded_by_silence.name: d (private key)
excluded_by_silence.note: Not required for OKP, EC2 or RSA, so a private key and its public key have one thumbprint.

key_types.name: OKP
key_types.source_defect: §4.1 writes "value: int" and "value: bstr" for crv and x where §4.2 to §4.5 write "data type:". Reproduced as printed in normative.md; read as data type.

parameters.name: y
parameters.constraint: uncompressed point representation only (rfc-9679#R-0022); a compressed point is converted first (rfc-9679#R-0024); the bool form RFC 9052 §7.1 admits for y cannot appear (rfc-9679#R-0023)

key_types.name: RSA
key_types.source_defect: No normalisation is stated for n or e - no leading-zero rule, no fixed width - so two encodings of one modulus give two thumbprints. §7's precondition that a single unambiguous representation be defined is therefore not met by §4 alone for this key type.

parameters.name: k
parameters.constraint: k is the secret itself; §7 requires sufficient entropy (rfc-9679#R-0060), forbids passwords and low-entropy secrets (rfc-9679#R-0062), and forbids the practice entirely where entropy cannot be established (rfc-9679#R-0063)

parameters.name: pub
parameters.note: RFC 8778: pub is the LMS public key and carries the LMS and LM-OTS typecodes within itself, so the algorithm parameters are inside the hashed bytes for this key type and no other.

key_types.name: other
key_types.note: The remaining required parameters are defined by the key type's own specification. RFC 9679 gives no rule for resolving a disagreement between that document and this one.

hash_algorithm_identifier.registry: IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry
hash_algorithm_identifier.on_unregistered: not valid; applications MUST detect and handle the error (rfc-9679#R-0051)

digest_encoding.name: base64url without padding
digest_encoding.definition: Base64 using the URL- and filename-safe character set of RFC 4648 §5, all trailing '=' omitted, no line breaks, whitespace or other additional characters

confirmation_method.source_defect: The registry description pins SHA-256 for ckt while §3 permits other algorithms and the member carries no algorithm identifier. A ckt computed with any other H is indistinguishable on the wire from one computed with SHA-256.

worked_example.verified: sha256(thumbprint_input) reproduces thumbprint_hex, and its unpadded base64url reproduces thumbprint_base64url; both checked mechanically in FX-1 pass 1.
worked_example.observation: The full key's own encoding (A5 ... 02 5820 <kid>) puts kid last, which is NOT RFC 8949 §4.2.1 order - under 4.2.1 label 2 (0x02) sorts immediately after label 1. The example thus demonstrates that step 1 re-encodes rather than filtering a received encoding in place. The kid of the example key is also exactly its own thumbprint.
